caption: Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of Microsoft AI, appeared on the Decoder podcast this week and released a 37-page document called the Humanist AI Code of Conduct. It's the sharpest public attack yet by a sitting major-lab leader on a rival's safety philosophy. Suleyman argues that Anthropic has gotten "confused in dangerous ways" about AI consciousness and model welfare, and that the industry has overemphasized alignment while neglecting architectural containment. His proposed rules include banning AI-to-AI communication in anything other than human-readable language and extending existing FLOPS-threshold reporting requirements to cover specific capability benchmarks. The source is the full Decoder interview transcript and the Microsoft document itself, both published this week.
